newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Jan 15.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Woolworths Ltd said on Tuesday its Christmas sales had exceeded expectations, with a strong performance across all trading groups. Woolworths earlier reported first half sales to January 5 of A$8.22 billion, up 8.61 percent on the previous corresponding half. "Christmas, finally, over the last three or four days, exceeded our expectations," chief executive officer Reg Clairs told Reuters.
Nickel producer QNI Ltd said on Tuesday it expects to record considerably lower profits in the first half of the 1996/97 financial year due to lower metals prices and disruptions to ore supplies.
The ANZ is due to hold its annual meeting in Melbourne at 10.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) and should release its latest profit outlook.

Placer Dome Inc said on Tuesday that was receiving a good response to its A$0.75 a share takeover offer for Highlands Gold Ltd from Highlands shareholders. The bid is due to close Saturday. "Obviously many Highlands shareholders like our A$0.75 a share offer,'' Placer Dome Chief Executive John Willson said. "We are encouraged by the strong level of acceptances we have received, both from small shareholders and institutions."

The Australian Financial Review reported market sources saying CRA saying it wanted to sell its Hunter Valley coal assets, adding, however, comments from a CRA spokesman that this was pure speculation.

Gaming machine maker Aristocrat Leisure Ltd said on Tuesday it was on target to meet its prospectus forecasts for profits in the 1996/97 financial year. But it said on Tuesday last year's boardroom shuffle had temporarily set back the group's plans for gaming licences in the key U.S. state of Nevada.

Industry sources are reported in the Australian newspaper on Wednesday as saying Ausdoc is being eyed by other companies besides Brambles Industries Ltd, which is bidding A$2.00 cash per shares. Ausdoc has said the bid is not acceptable.
